blocks.text: Linearizability means every operation appears to take effect atomically at one point in time, consistent with real-time order.

blocks.text: Else, when there is no partition, you trade Latency vs Consistency.
The limit: the order is only known after the fact.
The weakness is that 2PC blocks. If the coordinator dies, participants hold locks until it recovers. This is why microservices use sagas instead.
If the leader goes silent, a follower times out, increments the term, and asks for votes. A majority makes it leader. A higher term fences the old leader.
Membership via ephemeral nodes that vanish when a session dies; config and shard maps that clients watch for changes.

items: Answer per feature: booking and payment are CP, search and feeds are AP. Mention PACELC latency cost.
Not 2PC (blocking, coupling). Use a saga + outbox + idempotent consumers.
Leader election via ZooKeeper or etcd (consensus), lease + fencing token.
Needs linearizable compare-and-set: one strongly consistent store (Spanner, CockroachDB, or a single-leader region for usernames).
